reason: The text demonstrates agency exercised by multiple non-leader figures. Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah (royal officials) act decisively in negotiating and choosing to speak Aramaic rather than Hebrew. The Rabshakeh (an Assyrian official) delivers messages and makes rhetorical choices. The common people on the wall make a deliberate choice to remain silent. The sons of Sennacherib (Adrammelech and Sharezer) exercise agency by assassinating their father. Even an angel of God exercises agency by striking down 185,000 soldiers. The text repeatedly shows subordinate figures, common people, and supernatural beings making consequential decisions and taking action, not merely leaders.
